**Status: open design discussion. Implementation not started. Comments and alternative proposals welcome.**

## Proposal

A new CLI subcommand `sel2pw fill-stubs` that runs **after** the deterministic conversion pipeline. It reads `CONVERSION_REVIEW.md` from the output folder, locates each file in `tests/_legacy-stubs/`, prompts the configured LLM for a candidate body, and writes `<name>.filled.ts` next to the original stub with full provenance in a header comment.

### Why a two-pass split (not inline LLM fallback)

- Deterministic output stays pure. The user always sees exactly what the rule catalogue produced; the LLM never touches `pages/`, `tests/*.spec.ts`, or any other core artifact.
- LLM scope is bounded to one stub file per invocation — small inputs, small outputs, debuggable one at a time.
- Review-first workflow. User reads `CONVERSION_REVIEW.md`, decides whether the stubs are worth filling, THEN opts in.
- Auditable. Each filled file carries a header with provider, model, timestamp, input SHA, prompt SHA. If a suggestion is wrong, diff against the raw stub.
- Addresses the common concern that LLM-based migration drifts silently.

### Proposed CLI shape

```bash
# Pass 1 — deterministic (what we have today)
sel2pw convert ./my-selenium-suite --out ./pw

# Pass 2 — opt-in LLM stub-filler
sel2pw fill-stubs ./pw --provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-5

# Dry-run: see what WOULD be filled + token cost estimate, no API calls
sel2pw fill-stubs ./pw --dry-run

# Scope to specific files
sel2pw fill-stubs ./pw --only booking-data-factory,configuration-manager
```

### Output file header example

```ts
// Generated by sel2pw fill-stubs @ 2026-11-03T14:22Z
// Provider: anthropic   Model: claude-sonnet-5-20250929
// Input SHA: f8a9b2c1   Prompt SHA: 3e4d5f6a
// To accept, replace _legacy-stubs/booking-data-factory.ts with this file.
// Review carefully — this body was generated by a language model.
```

### What this unlocks

- An empirical study of LLM-assisted migration completion with reproducible provenance.
- Provider sensitivity measurements (Anthropic vs OpenAI vs Google) against the same 15-repo benchmark.
- A credible answer to "what does the LLM path actually add?" — a question users keep asking.

## Discussion needed before implementation

- Rate limiting + token budget UX
- How to validate suggested stub bodies (compile check? snapshot against hand-written?)
- Governance / privacy: `--redact` option to mask literals, class names, etc. before sending to the provider
- Default `--off` so a stray `fill-stubs` call never hits a paid API unexpectedly

Comments welcome. Hoping to land this in a v3.0 release in Q1 2027.
